hints.title: Follow the brackets from the inside
hints.body: The two square roots act on different quantities. In f, log2x=12log2x. In g, the square root applies to the whole quantity log2x.
hints.recap: Use the power rule on the quantity actually inside each logarithm.
hints.pause: Apply the outer logarithm in each expression separately.

hints.title: Give the shared expression one name
hints.body: Write z=log2(log2x). The product rule gives f=log2(12)+z=z−1, while the power rule gives g=12z.
hints.recap: A shared complicated expression can become a single variable.
hints.pitfall: The constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow></math> comes from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>; it is not an outside factor of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math>.
hints.pause: Find the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>z</mi></mrow></math> meet.

recall.reminder: Rename the repeated expression, then solve the simpler problem in the new variable.

hints.title: Compare on each side of the meeting point
hints.body: Solve where the two linear expressions agree. Compare their values on either side, and track the common output at the crossing.
hints.recap: The crossing separates the two possible orderings.
hints.pitfall: The input at the crossing and the common output are different quantities.
hints.pause: Derive both chains of inequalities, include equality, and match the complete statement.

recall.reminder: The crossing separates the two possible orderings.

solution:
Let z=log2(log2x). Since x>1, this quantity is defined and can take any real value.

Then f=log2(12log2x)=z−1 and g=log2((log2x)1/2)=z/2.

They meet at z=2, with f=g=1. If z≥2, then 1≤g≤f. If z≤2, then f≤g≤1. At the crossing both statements hold, which is allowed by inclusive “or”. Answer F.
knowledgePattern: Linearise nested logarithms to order two functions
